pairs.he: השבטים סברו שרוצה למשול במלוכה דס״א שנמשך מעשירות, ובאמת להיפך ממשלתו על ידי הדעת שזוכין ע״י להארת הרצון שזוכים באכילה, ולכן יהודה הציע שע״י שימכרו אותו יתקנו פגם הארת הרצון לפי דעתם
pairs.en: The tribes thought that he wanted to rule with the kingship of the sitra achra, which proceeds from wealth; but in truth it is the reverse: his rule is through knowledge, through which one merits the illumination of will that is attained in eating. And therefore Yehudah proposed that by selling him they would rectify the blemish in the illumination of will, according to their understanding.

pairs.he: ״מַה בֶּצַע כִּי נַהֲרֹג אֶת אָחִינוּ״ (ל״ז, כו) עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה כִּי מְרַחֲמָם יְנַהֲגֵם בְּלִקּוּטֵי תִנְיָנָא סִימָן ז, עַיֵּן שָׁם. מְבֹאָר שָׁם שֶׁעִקַּר הַחִיּוּב מַה שֶּׁהָאָדָם מְחֻיָּב לְהַשְׁאִיר אַחֲרָיו אֶת ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכוּ׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם מֵעִנְיַן בֵּן וְתַלְמִיד שֶׁעַל יָדָם נִשְׁאָר דַּעְתּוֹ בָּעוֹלָם שֶׁזֶּה עִקַּר הִשָּׁאֲרוּתוֹ, כִּי אֵין נִשְׁאָר מֵהָאָדָם אַחַר מוֹתוֹ שׁוּם דָּבָר כִּי אִם הַדַּעַת שֶׁהֵאִיר בְּבָנִים וְתַלְמִידִים וְכוּ׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם כָּל זֶה הֵיטֵב.
pairs.en: “What profit is there if we kill our brother?” (37:26), according to the teaching “For their compassionate One shall guide them,” in Likutay Tinyana, section 7; see there. It is explained there that the chief obligation, that which a person is obligated to leave after him, is Hashem, blessed be He, etc.; see there concerning a son and a disciple, through whom his knowledge remains in the world, which is his principal enduring remnant. For nothing remains of a person after his death except the knowledge he illuminated in children and disciples, etc.; see all this there carefully.

pairs.he: וּמְבֹאָר שָׁם שֶׁעַל יְדֵי כְּלָלִיּוּת בֵּן וְתַלְמִיד עַל יְדֵי זֶה מִי שֶׁהוּא אִישׁ חַיִל יָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל בְּעֵת הָאֲכִילָה הֶאָרַת הָרָצוֹן וְכוּ׳, כִּי עִקַּר הַפַּרְנָסָה נִמְשָׁךְ מִיָּם הַחָכְמָה שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ עַל יְדֵי בֵּן וְתַלְמִיד וְכוּ׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם כָּל זֶה הֵיטֵב.
pairs.en: And it is explained there that through the incorporation of son and disciple, thereby one who is a man of valor can receive the illumination of will while eating, etc.; for sustenance is principally drawn from the sea of wisdom, which is drawn through son and disciple, etc.; see all this there carefully.

pairs.he: יַעֲקֹב מָסַר הַבְּכוֹרָה לִבְנוֹ לְיוֹסֵף, כִּי בֶן זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ, וְזֶהוּ זָקֵן קָנָה חָכְמָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה. וּמוּבָא בְּפֵרוּשׁ רש״י שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁלָּמַד מִשֵּׁם וְעֵבֶר מָסַר לוֹ. וְעַל כֵּן מֵחֲמַת שֶׁמָּסַר לוֹ חָכְמָתוֹ וְדַעְתּוֹ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה עַל כֵּן מָסַר לוֹ הַבְּכוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת קְדֻשַּׁת הַדַּעַת שֶׁהַצַּדִּיק צָרִיךְ לְהַשְׁאִיר לְבָנָיו וּלְתַלְמִידָיו כַּנַּ״ל, כִּי הַבְּכוֹרָה הָיְתָה מַגִּיעַ לִרְאוּבֵן. אַךְ בְּחַלְּלוֹ יְצוּעֵי אָבִיו וְזֶה פְּגַם בְּהַדַּעַת עַל יְדֵי זֶה נָתַן בְּכוֹרָתוֹ לְיוֹסֵף שֶׁזָּכָה לִשְׁמֹר הַדַּעַת בִּשְׁלֵמוּת, כִּי עָמַד בְּנִסָּיוֹן שֶׁל תַּאֲוָה זֹאת שֶׁזֶּה עִקַּר שְׁמִירַת הַדַּעַת.
pairs.en: Yaakov handed the birthright to his son, to Yosef, for “he was a son of old age to him”; and this is “an elder”—one who has acquired wisdom, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said. And it is cited in Rashi’s commentary that everything he learned from Shem and Ever he handed over to him. And therefore, because he handed his wisdom and holy knowledge over to him, therefore he handed the birthright over to him, which is the aspect of the holiness of the knowledge that the tzaddik must leave to his children and disciples, as above. For the birthright was due to Reuven, but when he profaned his father’s couch, and this is a blemish in knowledge, through this he gave his birthright to Yosef, who merited to preserve knowledge completely, for he stood firm in the trial of this desire, which is the chief preservation of knowledge.

pairs.he: וְהַשְּׁבָטִים הִתְקַנְּאוּ בוֹ עַל שֶׁהוֹצִיא דִבָּה עֲלֵיהֶם. עַל כֵּן חָשְׁדוּ אוֹתוֹ עַל כָּל הַדְּבָרִים שֶׁדִּבֵּר עֲלֵיהֶם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה כָּל הַפּוֹסֵל בְּמוּמוֹ פּוֹסֵל. גַּם נִסְתַּכְּלוּ בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁיֵּצְאוּ מִמֶּנּוּ יָרָבְעָם וְאַחְאָב שֶׁיַּעֲבִדוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה. עַל כֵּן חָשְׁדוּ אוֹתוֹ שֶׁמַּטְעֶה אֶת אָבִיו כְּמוֹ עֵשָׂו עַד שֶׁהִתִּירוּ אֶת דָּמוֹ.
pairs.en: And the tribes became jealous of him because he brought an evil report about them. Therefore they suspected him of all the things he spoke against them, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: whoever disqualifies, disqualifies through his own blemish. They also saw through the holy spirit that Yeravam and Achav would emerge from him and would serve idolatry. Therefore they suspected him of misleading his father like Esav, until they permitted his blood [to be shed].

pairs.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת הַחֲלוֹם שֶׁסִּפֵּר לָהֶם, וְהִנֵּה אֲנַחְנוּ מְאַלְּמִים אֲלֻמִּים וְכוּ׳ וְהִנֵּה קָמָה אֲלֻמָּתִי וְגַם נִצָּבָה וְכוּ׳. וַיֹּאמְרוּ לוֹ אֶחָיו הֲמָלֹךְ תִּמְלֹךְ עָלֵינוּ אִם וְכוּ׳, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת טָעוּ אֶחָיו בְּיוֹסֵף, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה צַדִּיק גָּדוֹל וְזָכָה לְקַבֵּל עִקַּר הַדַּעַת מֵאָבִיו. וְעַל כֵּן הֶרְאוּ לוֹ בַּחֲלוֹם שֶׁיִּמְלֹךְ וְיִמְשֹׁל, וְהֶרְאוּ לוֹ דַּיְקָא עַל יְדֵי תְּבוּאוֹת הַשָּׂדֶה שֶׁהָיָה מְאַלְּמִים אֲלֻמִּים, הַיְנוּ עִנְיָן הַנַּ״ל שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַדַּעַת זוֹכִין לְקַבֵּל הֶאָרַת הָרָצוֹן עַל יְדֵי הַמְּלוּכָה וְהַמֶּמְשָׁלָה.
pairs.en: And this is the aspect of the dream he told them: “And behold, we were binding sheaves,” etc., “and behold, my sheaf arose and also stood upright,” etc. And his brothers said to him, “Will you indeed reign over us, or,” etc. For in truth his brothers were mistaken about Yosef, for in truth he was a great tzaddik and merited to receive the principal knowledge from his father. And therefore they showed him in a dream that he would reign and rule, and they showed him specifically through the produce of the field, for they were binding sheaves: namely, the aforesaid matter, that through knowledge one merits to receive the illumination of will through kingship and rule.

pairs.he: עַל כֵּן הֶרְאוּ לוֹ שֶׁזָּכָה לָזֶה וְרָמְזוּ לוֹ דַּיְקָא בַּאֲלֻמּוֹת הַשָּׂדֶה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שֶׁפַע הַפַּרְנָסָה לְהוֹרוֹת שֶׁהוּא זָכָה לְמֶמְשָׁלָה וּמְלוּכָה שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה גְּדֵלִים אֲלֻמּוֹת הַשָּׂדֶה, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁפַע הַפַּרְנָסָה וְכוּ׳, וְזָכָה לָזֶה עַל יְדֵי גֹּדֶל הַדַּעַת הַנַּ״ל שֶׁקִּבֵּל מֵאָבִיו כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: Therefore they showed him that he merited this, and hinted to him specifically by the sheaves of the field, which are the aspect of the flow of sustenance, to indicate that he merited rule and kingship, through which the sheaves of the field grow—that is, the flow of sustenance, etc.—and he merited this through the greatness of the aforesaid knowledge that he received from his father, as above.

qualifiedAfter.en: Therefore they showed him that he merited this, and hinted to him specifically by the sheaves of the field, which are the aspect of the flow of sustenance, to indicate that he merited rule and kingship, through which the sheaves of the field grow—that is, the flow of sustenance, etc.—and he merited this through the greatness of the aforesaid knowledge that he received from his father, as above.

pairs.he: וְאֶחָיו הֵבִינוּ דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁפָּתַר הַחֲלוֹם בְּעִנְיָן זֶה, עַל כֵּן הִתְקַנְּאוּ בוֹ וְאָמְרוּ לוֹ, הֲמָלֹךְ תִּמְלֹךְ עָלֵינוּ וְכוּ׳. כִּי אָמְרוּ שֶׁהוּא בַּהֵפֶךְ שֶׁמַּטְעֶה אֶת אָבִיו וְרוֹצֶה לִמְשֹׁל וְלִמְלֹךְ בְּמַלְכוּת דְּסִטְרָא אַחֲרָא כְּמוֹ יָרָבְעָם שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁמָּלַךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהֶחֱטִיא אוֹתָם מְאֹד עַל יְדֵי שְׁנֵי עֶגְלֵי זָהָב שֶׁעָשָׂה לָהֶם.
pairs.en: And his brothers understood his intention, that he interpreted the dream in this sense. Therefore they became jealous of him and said to him, “Will you indeed reign over us,” etc. For they said that it was the reverse: that he was misleading his father and wanted to rule and reign with the kingship of the sitra achra, like Yeravam who emerged from him, who reigned over Israel and caused them to sin greatly through the two golden calves he made for them.

pairs.he: כִּי בְּהַמָּמוֹן וְהָעֲשִׁירוּת בִּקְדֻשָּׁה גָּבֹהַּ מְאֹד מְאֹד, כִּי נִמְשָׁךְ מֵהַיָּדַיִם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיָם הַחָכְמָה וְכוּ׳ וְעַל כֵּן מֵאִיר שָׁם הֶאָרַת הָרָצוֹן כַּנַּ״ל, אֲבָל זֶה אֵין זוֹכֶה כִּי אִם הַצַּדִּיק הָאֱמֶת וְהַנִּלְוִים אֵלָיו בֶּאֱמֶת שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִים דַּעְתּוֹ הַנַּ״ל שֶׁמֵּאִיר בְּבֵן וְתַלְמִיד כַּנַּ״ל, אֲבָל לְהֵפֶךְ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם מִי שֶׁאֵין מְקַבֵּל הַדַּעַת הַנַּ״ל, מִכָּל שֶׁכֵּן מִי שֶׁחוֹלֵק עַל הַצַּדִּיק הַזֶּה שֶׁמֵּאִיר הַדַּעַת הַנַּ״ל כָּל נְפִילָתוֹ הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַמָּמוֹן וְהָעֲשִׁירוּת, כִּי לְמַטָּה נֶאֱחָזִים כָּל הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּהַמָּמוֹן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר (בסימן כג) כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב, וְכֶסֶף הִרְבֵּיתִי לָהֶם וְזָהָב עָשׂוּ לַבָּעַל (עין מזה במקום אחר) וְעַל כֵּן טָעוּ הַשְּׁבָטִים וְאָמְרוּ שֶׁיוֹסֵף רוֹצֶה לִמְלֹךְ עֲלֵיהֶם בְּמַלְכוּת הַסִּטְרָא אַחֲרָא הַנַּ״ל עַד שֶׁהִתִּירוּ אֶת דָּמוֹ.
pairs.en: For in money and wealth in holiness [the level] is very, very high, for it proceeds from the hands that are in the sea of wisdom, etc., and therefore the illumination of will shines there, as above. But none merits this except the true tzaddik and those who genuinely join him, who receive his aforesaid knowledge that he illuminates in son and disciple, as above. But conversely, God forbid, whoever does not receive the aforesaid knowledge, and all the more whoever disputes this tzaddik who illuminates the aforesaid knowledge—all his downfall is through money and wealth, for below, this entire world clings to money, as written elsewhere (in section 23), as it is written, “And I increased silver for them, and gold they made for Baal” (see concerning this elsewhere). And therefore the tribes erred and said that Yosef wanted to reign over them with the aforesaid kingship of the sitra achra, until they permitted his blood [to be shed].

qualifiedAfter.en: For in money and wealth in holiness [the level] is very, very high, for it proceeds from the hands that are in the sea of wisdom, etc., and therefore the illumination of will shines there, as above. But none merits this except the true tzaddik and those who genuinely join him, who receive his aforesaid knowledge that he illuminates in son and disciple, as above. But conversely, God forbid, whoever does not receive the aforesaid knowledge, and all the more whoever disputes this tzaddik who illuminates the aforesaid knowledge—all his downfall is through money and wealth, for below, this entire world clings to money, as written elsewhere (in section 23), as it is written, “And I increased silver for them, and gold they made for Baal” (see concerning this elsewhere). And therefore the tribes erred and said that Yosef wanted to reign over them with the aforesaid kingship of the sitra achra, until they permitted his blood [to be shed].

pairs.he: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם יְהוּדָה, מַה בֶּצַע כִּי נַהֲרֹג אֶת אָחִינוּ וְכוּ׳ לְכוּ וְנִמְכְּרֶנּוּ לַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִים וְכוּ׳. וְהַדָּבָר תָּמוּהַּ מְאֹד וְכִי עָלָה עַל דַּעַת יְהוּדָה שֶׁרוֹצִים לַהֲרֹג אֶת יוֹסֵף בִּשְׁבִיל בֶּצַע וּמָמוֹן, עַד שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם מַה בֶּצַע כִּי נַהֲרֹג וְכוּ׳, הֲלֹא יָדַע הָאֱמֶת שֶׁכַּוָּנָתָם לְשָׁמַיִם לְפִי טָעוּתָם שֶׁרוֹצִים לַהֲרְגוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יַטְעֶה אוֹתָם אוֹ אֲחֵרִים מֵהָאֱמוּנָה הָאֲמִתִּית שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ מֵאֲבִיהֶם, אֲבָל עַל כָּל פָּנִים חַס וְשָׁלוֹם אֵין כַּוָּנָתָם כְּלָל בִּשְׁבִיל אֵיזֶה מָמוֹן וּבֶצַע.
pairs.en: And this is what Yehudah said to them: “What profit is there if we kill our brother,” etc., “Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites,” etc. And the matter is most astonishing: did it enter Yehudah’s mind that they wanted to kill Yosef for profit and money, so that he said to them, “What profit is there if we kill,” etc.? Did he not know the truth, that their intention was for Heaven, according to their error, that they wanted to kill him so that he would not mislead them or others away from the true faith they received from their father? But in any event, God forbid, their intention was not at all for any money and profit.

pairs.he: רַק יְהוּדָה רָמַז לָהֶם עִנְיָן הַנַּ״ל, מֵחֲמַת שֶׁלְּפִי דַּעְתְּכֶם רְצוֹנְכֶם לְבַעֲרוֹ כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְקַלְקֵל אֶת הַדַּעַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁהִתְחִילוּ הָאָבוֹת לְהַמְשִׁיךְ בָּעוֹלָם. וַאֲזַי הוּכְלוּ אַתֶּם לְהַמְשִׁיךְ זֶה הַדַּעַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ, עַל כֵּן אָמַר לָהֶם מַה בֶּצַע וְכוּ׳ לְכוּ וְנִמְכְּרֶנּוּ וְכוּ׳, הַיְנוּ שֶׁלְּפִי זֶה טוֹב לְמָכְרוֹ וּלְקַבֵּל בַּעֲדוֹ מָמוֹן, וְאַתֶּם הַשְּׁבָטִים שֶׁכֻּלְּכֶם קְדוֹשִׁים, כְּשֶׁתְּקַבְּלוּ מָמוֹן בַּעֲדוֹ וּתְקַבְּלוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה הֶאָרַת הָרָצוֹן שֶׁמֵּאִיר בְּהַמָּמוֹן כְּשֶׁמְּקַבְּלִים אוֹתוֹ כָּרָאוּי וַאֲזַי תְּתַקְּנוּ הַדָּבָר כָּרָאוּי.
pairs.en: Rather, Yehudah hinted to them at the aforesaid matter: since, according to your understanding, your wish was to remove him so that he would not corrupt the holy knowledge that the forefathers began to draw into the world, and then you would be able to draw this holy knowledge, therefore he said to them, “What profit,” etc., “Come, let us sell him,” etc. That is, according to this it is good to sell him and receive money for him; and you, the tribes, who are all holy, when you receive money for him and thereby receive the illumination of will that shines in money when it is received properly, then you will rectify the matter properly.

pairs.he: כִּי מַה שֶּׁלְּפִי דַּעְתְּכֶם רָצָה יוֹסֵף לִפְגֹּם בְּהַדַּעַת הַנַּ״ל שֶׁהוּא פְּגַם הָרָצוֹן הַמֵּאִיר בְּהַמָּמוֹן שֶׁהוּא פְּגַם הַמַּלְכוּת וְהַמֶּמְשָׁלָה, עַל כֵּן טוֹב שֶׁתִּמְכְּרוּ אוֹתוֹ וּבָזֶה תַּפִּילוּ אוֹתוֹ מֵהַמֶּמְשָׁלָה וְשׁוּב לֹא יוּכַל לִמְלֹךְ עֲלֵיכֶם בְּמַלְכוּת דְּסִטְרָא אַחֲרָא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם וּלְקַלְקֵל אֶת הַדַּעַת עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי הָעֲשִׁירוּת כְּמוֹ יָרָבְעָם וְכוּ׳, אַדְּרַבָּא, תְּקַבְּלוּ דְּמֵי מְכִירָתוֹ וְאָז תּוּכְלוּ לְקַבֵּל וּלְהַעֲלוֹת הֶאָרַת הָרָצוֹן שֶׁנָּפַל אֵצֶל יוֹסֵף לְפִי טָעוּתָם, וְאַתֶּם תַּעֲלוּ אוֹתוֹ וּתְקַבְּלוּ הֶאָרַת הָרָצוֹן עַל יְדֵי הַמָּמוֹן שֶׁתְּקַבְּלוּ בִּדְמֵי מְכִירָתוֹ.
pairs.en: For what, according to your understanding, Yosef wanted to blemish in the aforesaid knowledge is a blemish in the will that shines in money, which is a blemish in kingship and rule. Therefore it is good for you to sell him, and by this you will cast him down from rule, and he will no longer be able to reign over you with the kingship of the sitra achra, God forbid, and to corrupt knowledge through an abundance of wealth, like Yeravam, etc. On the contrary, you will receive the money from his sale, and then you will be able to receive and raise the illumination of will that fell with Yosef, according to their error; and you will raise it and receive the illumination of will through the money that you will receive as the price of his sale.

השבטים סברו שרוצה למשול במלוכה דס״א שנמשך מעשירות, ובאמת להיפך ממשלתו על ידי הדעת שזוכין ע״י להארת הרצון שזוכים באכילה, ולכן יהודה הציע שע״י שימכרו אותו יתקנו פגם הארת הרצון לפי דעתם

״מַה בֶּצַע כִּי נַהֲרֹג אֶת אָחִינוּ״ (ל״ז, כו) עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה כִּי מְרַחֲמָם יְנַהֲגֵם בְּלִקּוּטֵי תִנְיָנָא סִימָן ז, עַיֵּן שָׁם. מְבֹאָר שָׁם שֶׁעִקַּר הַחִיּוּב מַה שֶּׁהָאָדָם מְחֻיָּב לְהַשְׁאִיר אַחֲרָיו אֶת ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכוּ׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם מֵעִנְיַן בֵּן וְתַלְמִיד שֶׁעַל יָדָם נִשְׁאָר דַּעְתּוֹ בָּעוֹלָם שֶׁזֶּה עִקַּר הִשָּׁאֲרוּתוֹ, כִּי אֵין נִשְׁאָר מֵהָאָדָם אַחַר מוֹתוֹ שׁוּם דָּבָר כִּי אִם הַדַּעַת שֶׁהֵאִיר בְּבָנִים וְתַלְמִידִים וְכוּ׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם כָּל זֶה הֵיטֵב.

וּמְבֹאָר שָׁם שֶׁעַל יְדֵי כְּלָלִיּוּת בֵּן וְתַלְמִיד עַל יְדֵי זֶה מִי שֶׁהוּא אִישׁ חַיִל יָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל בְּעֵת הָאֲכִילָה הֶאָרַת הָרָצוֹן וְכוּ׳, כִּי עִקַּר הַפַּרְנָסָה נִמְשָׁךְ מִיָּם הַחָכְמָה שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ עַל יְדֵי בֵּן וְתַלְמִיד וְכוּ׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם כָּל זֶה הֵיטֵב.

יַעֲקֹב מָסַר הַבְּכוֹרָה לִבְנוֹ לְיוֹסֵף, כִּי בֶן זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ, וְזֶהוּ זָקֵן קָנָה חָכְמָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה. וּמוּבָא בְּפֵרוּשׁ רש״י שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁלָּמַד מִשֵּׁם וְעֵבֶר מָסַר לוֹ. וְעַל כֵּן מֵחֲמַת שֶׁמָּסַר לוֹ חָכְמָתוֹ וְדַעְתּוֹ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה עַל כֵּן מָסַר לוֹ הַבְּכוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת קְדֻשַּׁת הַדַּעַת שֶׁהַצַּדִּיק צָרִיךְ לְהַשְׁאִיר לְבָנָיו וּלְתַלְמִידָיו כַּנַּ״ל, כִּי הַבְּכוֹרָה הָיְתָה מַגִּיעַ לִרְאוּבֵן. אַךְ בְּחַלְּלוֹ יְצוּעֵי אָבִיו וְזֶה פְּגַם בְּהַדַּעַת עַל יְדֵי זֶה נָתַן בְּכוֹרָתוֹ לְיוֹסֵף שֶׁזָּכָה לִשְׁמֹר הַדַּעַת בִּשְׁלֵמוּת, כִּי עָמַד בְּנִסָּיוֹן שֶׁל תַּאֲוָה זֹאת שֶׁזֶּה עִקַּר שְׁמִירַת הַדַּעַת.

וְהַשְּׁבָטִים הִתְקַנְּאוּ בוֹ עַל שֶׁהוֹצִיא דִבָּה עֲלֵיהֶם. עַל כֵּן חָשְׁדוּ אוֹתוֹ עַל כָּל הַדְּבָרִים שֶׁדִּבֵּר עֲלֵיהֶם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה כָּל הַפּוֹסֵל בְּמוּמוֹ פּוֹסֵל. גַּם נִסְתַּכְּלוּ בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁיֵּצְאוּ מִמֶּנּוּ יָרָבְעָם וְאַחְאָב שֶׁיַּעֲבִדוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה. עַל כֵּן חָשְׁדוּ אוֹתוֹ שֶׁמַּטְעֶה אֶת אָבִיו כְּמוֹ עֵשָׂו עַד שֶׁהִתִּירוּ אֶת דָּמוֹ.

וְזֶה בְּחִינַת הַחֲלוֹם שֶׁסִּפֵּר לָהֶם, וְהִנֵּה אֲנַחְנוּ מְאַלְּמִים אֲלֻמִּים וְכוּ׳ וְהִנֵּה קָמָה אֲלֻמָּתִי וְגַם נִצָּבָה וְכוּ׳. וַיֹּאמְרוּ לוֹ אֶחָיו הֲמָלֹךְ תִּמְלֹךְ עָלֵינוּ אִם וְכוּ׳, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת טָעוּ אֶחָיו בְּיוֹסֵף, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה צַדִּיק גָּדוֹל וְזָכָה לְקַבֵּל עִקַּר הַדַּעַת מֵאָבִיו. וְעַל כֵּן הֶרְאוּ לוֹ בַּחֲלוֹם שֶׁיִּמְלֹךְ וְיִמְשֹׁל, וְהֶרְאוּ לוֹ דַּיְקָא עַל יְדֵי תְּבוּאוֹת הַשָּׂדֶה שֶׁהָיָה מְאַלְּמִים אֲלֻמִּים, הַיְנוּ עִנְיָן הַנַּ״ל שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַדַּעַת זוֹכִין לְקַבֵּל הֶאָרַת הָרָצוֹן עַל יְדֵי הַמְּלוּכָה וְהַמֶּמְשָׁלָה.

עַל כֵּן הֶרְאוּ לוֹ שֶׁזָּכָה לָזֶה וְרָמְזוּ לוֹ דַּיְקָא בַּאֲלֻמּוֹת הַשָּׂדֶה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שֶׁפַע הַפַּרְנָסָה לְהוֹרוֹת שֶׁהוּא זָכָה לְמֶמְשָׁלָה וּמְלוּכָה שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה גְּדֵלִים אֲלֻמּוֹת הַשָּׂדֶה, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁפַע הַפַּרְנָסָה וְכוּ׳, וְזָכָה לָזֶה עַל יְדֵי גֹּדֶל הַדַּעַת הַנַּ״ל שֶׁקִּבֵּל מֵאָבִיו כַּנַּ״ל.

וְאֶחָיו הֵבִינוּ דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁפָּתַר הַחֲלוֹם בְּעִנְיָן זֶה, עַל כֵּן הִתְקַנְּאוּ בוֹ וְאָמְרוּ לוֹ, הֲמָלֹךְ תִּמְלֹךְ עָלֵינוּ וְכוּ׳. כִּי אָמְרוּ שֶׁהוּא בַּהֵפֶךְ שֶׁמַּטְעֶה אֶת אָבִיו וְרוֹצֶה לִמְשֹׁל וְלִמְלֹךְ בְּמַלְכוּת דְּסִטְרָא אַחֲרָא כְּמוֹ יָרָבְעָם שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁמָּלַךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהֶחֱטִיא אוֹתָם מְאֹד עַל יְדֵי שְׁנֵי עֶגְלֵי זָהָב שֶׁעָשָׂה לָהֶם.

כִּי בְּהַמָּמוֹן וְהָעֲשִׁירוּת בִּקְדֻשָּׁה גָּבֹהַּ מְאֹד מְאֹד, כִּי נִמְשָׁךְ מֵהַיָּדַיִם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיָם הַחָכְמָה וְכוּ׳ וְעַל כֵּן מֵאִיר שָׁם הֶאָרַת הָרָצוֹן כַּנַּ״ל, אֲבָל זֶה אֵין זוֹכֶה כִּי אִם הַצַּדִּיק הָאֱמֶת וְהַנִּלְוִים אֵלָיו בֶּאֱמֶת שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִים דַּעְתּוֹ הַנַּ״ל שֶׁמֵּאִיר בְּבֵן וְתַלְמִיד כַּנַּ״ל, אֲבָל לְהֵפֶךְ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם מִי שֶׁאֵין מְקַבֵּל הַדַּעַת הַנַּ״ל, מִכָּל שֶׁכֵּן מִי שֶׁחוֹלֵק עַל הַצַּדִּיק הַזֶּה שֶׁמֵּאִיר הַדַּעַת הַנַּ״ל כָּל נְפִילָתוֹ הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַמָּמוֹן וְהָעֲשִׁירוּת, כִּי לְמַטָּה נֶאֱחָזִים כָּל הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּהַמָּמוֹן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר (בסימן כג) כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב, וְכֶסֶף הִרְבֵּיתִי לָהֶם וְזָהָב עָשׂוּ לַבָּעַל (עין מזה במקום אחר) וְעַל כֵּן טָעוּ הַשְּׁבָטִים וְאָמְרוּ שֶׁיוֹסֵף רוֹצֶה לִמְלֹךְ עֲלֵיהֶם בְּמַלְכוּת הַסִּטְרָא אַחֲרָא הַנַּ״ל עַד שֶׁהִתִּירוּ אֶת דָּמוֹ.

וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם יְהוּדָה, מַה בֶּצַע כִּי נַהֲרֹג אֶת אָחִינוּ וְכוּ׳ לְכוּ וְנִמְכְּרֶנּוּ לַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִים וְכוּ׳. וְהַדָּבָר תָּמוּהַּ מְאֹד וְכִי עָלָה עַל דַּעַת יְהוּדָה שֶׁרוֹצִים לַהֲרֹג אֶת יוֹסֵף בִּשְׁבִיל בֶּצַע וּמָמוֹן, עַד שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם מַה בֶּצַע כִּי נַהֲרֹג וְכוּ׳, הֲלֹא יָדַע הָאֱמֶת שֶׁכַּוָּנָתָם לְשָׁמַיִם לְפִי טָעוּתָם שֶׁרוֹצִים לַהֲרְגוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יַטְעֶה אוֹתָם אוֹ אֲחֵרִים מֵהָאֱמוּנָה הָאֲמִתִּית שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ מֵאֲבִיהֶם, אֲבָל עַל כָּל פָּנִים חַס וְשָׁלוֹם אֵין כַּוָּנָתָם כְּלָל בִּשְׁבִיל אֵיזֶה מָמוֹן וּבֶצַע.

רַק יְהוּדָה רָמַז לָהֶם עִנְיָן הַנַּ״ל, מֵחֲמַת שֶׁלְּפִי דַּעְתְּכֶם רְצוֹנְכֶם לְבַעֲרוֹ כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְקַלְקֵל אֶת הַדַּעַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁהִתְחִילוּ הָאָבוֹת לְהַמְשִׁיךְ בָּעוֹלָם. וַאֲזַי הוּכְלוּ אַתֶּם לְהַמְשִׁיךְ זֶה הַדַּעַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ, עַל כֵּן אָמַר לָהֶם מַה בֶּצַע וְכוּ׳ לְכוּ וְנִמְכְּרֶנּוּ וְכוּ׳, הַיְנוּ שֶׁלְּפִי זֶה טוֹב לְמָכְרוֹ וּלְקַבֵּל בַּעֲדוֹ מָמוֹן, וְאַתֶּם הַשְּׁבָטִים שֶׁכֻּלְּכֶם קְדוֹשִׁים, כְּשֶׁתְּקַבְּלוּ מָמוֹן בַּעֲדוֹ וּתְקַבְּלוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה הֶאָרַת הָרָצוֹן שֶׁמֵּאִיר בְּהַמָּמוֹן כְּשֶׁמְּקַבְּלִים אוֹתוֹ כָּרָאוּי וַאֲזַי תְּתַקְּנוּ הַדָּבָר כָּרָאוּי.

כִּי מַה שֶּׁלְּפִי דַּעְתְּכֶם רָצָה יוֹסֵף לִפְגֹּם בְּהַדַּעַת הַנַּ״ל שֶׁהוּא פְּגַם הָרָצוֹן הַמֵּאִיר בְּהַמָּמוֹן שֶׁהוּא פְּגַם הַמַּלְכוּת וְהַמֶּמְשָׁלָה, עַל כֵּן טוֹב שֶׁתִּמְכְּרוּ אוֹתוֹ וּבָזֶה תַּפִּילוּ אוֹתוֹ מֵהַמֶּמְשָׁלָה וְשׁוּב לֹא יוּכַל לִמְלֹךְ עֲלֵיכֶם בְּמַלְכוּת דְּסִטְרָא אַחֲרָא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם וּלְקַלְקֵל אֶת הַדַּעַת עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי הָעֲשִׁירוּת כְּמוֹ יָרָבְעָם וְכוּ׳, אַדְּרַבָּא, תְּקַבְּלוּ דְּמֵי מְכִירָתוֹ וְאָז תּוּכְלוּ לְקַבֵּל וּלְהַעֲלוֹת הֶאָרַת הָרָצוֹן שֶׁנָּפַל אֵצֶל יוֹסֵף לְפִי טָעוּתָם, וְאַתֶּם תַּעֲלוּ אוֹתוֹ וּתְקַבְּלוּ הֶאָרַת הָרָצוֹן עַל יְדֵי הַמָּמוֹן שֶׁתְּקַבְּלוּ בִּדְמֵי מְכִירָתוֹ.

(הלכות פדיון בכור הלכה ה׳ אות י״ד)
breslov.en:
The tribes thought that he wanted to rule with the kingship of the sitra achra, which proceeds from wealth; but in truth it is the reverse: his rule is through knowledge, through which one merits the illumination of will that is attained in eating. And therefore Yehudah proposed that by selling him they would rectify the blemish in the illumination of will, according to their understanding.

“What profit is there if we kill our brother?” (37:26), according to the teaching “For their compassionate One shall guide them,” in Likutay Tinyana, section 7; see there. It is explained there that the chief obligation, that which a person is obligated to leave after him, is Hashem, blessed be He, etc.; see there concerning a son and a disciple, through whom his knowledge remains in the world, which is his principal enduring remnant. For nothing remains of a person after his death except the knowledge he illuminated in children and disciples, etc.; see all this there carefully.

And it is explained there that through the incorporation of son and disciple, thereby one who is a man of valor can receive the illumination of will while eating, etc.; for sustenance is principally drawn from the sea of wisdom, which is drawn through son and disciple, etc.; see all this there carefully.

Yaakov handed the birthright to his son, to Yosef, for “he was a son of old age to him”; and this is “an elder”—one who has acquired wisdom, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said. And it is cited in Rashi’s commentary that everything he learned from Shem and Ever he handed over to him. And therefore, because he handed his wisdom and holy knowledge over to him, therefore he handed the birthright over to him, which is the aspect of the holiness of the knowledge that the tzaddik must leave to his children and disciples, as above. For the birthright was due to Reuven, but when he profaned his father’s couch, and this is a blemish in knowledge, through this he gave his birthright to Yosef, who merited to preserve knowledge completely, for he stood firm in the trial of this desire, which is the chief preservation of knowledge.

And the tribes became jealous of him because he brought an evil report about them. Therefore they suspected him of all the things he spoke against them, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: whoever disqualifies, disqualifies through his own blemish. They also saw through the holy spirit that Yeravam and Achav would emerge from him and would serve idolatry. Therefore they suspected him of misleading his father like Esav, until they permitted his blood [to be shed].

And this is the aspect of the dream he told them: “And behold, we were binding sheaves,” etc., “and behold, my sheaf arose and also stood upright,” etc. And his brothers said to him, “Will you indeed reign over us, or,” etc. For in truth his brothers were mistaken about Yosef, for in truth he was a great tzaddik and merited to receive the principal knowledge from his father. And therefore they showed him in a dream that he would reign and rule, and they showed him specifically through the produce of the field, for they were binding sheaves: namely, the aforesaid matter, that through knowledge one merits to receive the illumination of will through kingship and rule.

Therefore they showed him that he merited this, and hinted to him specifically by the sheaves of the field, which are the aspect of the flow of sustenance, to indicate that he merited rule and kingship, through which the sheaves of the field grow—that is, the flow of sustenance, etc.—and he merited this through the greatness of the aforesaid knowledge that he received from his father, as above.

And his brothers understood his intention, that he interpreted the dream in this sense. And this is what Yehudah said to them: “What profit is there if we kill our brother,” etc., “Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites,” etc. And the matter is most astonishing: did it enter Yehudah’s mind that they wanted to kill Yosef for profit and money, so that he said to them, “What profit is there if we kill,” etc.? pairs.en: The holy gaon Rabbi Hirsch Michel Shapira, of blessed memory, wrote in Tzvi LaTzaddik (letter 3): Since the people of the Lord have separated into various societies and factions, it is true that they are all holy, and they all wish to serve the Lord and to understand the depths of our holy Torah and the order of the proper, pure service. And each and every society delves, in the purity of their hearts, to find for themselves and for others a way and a path to hold fast wholeheartedly to our Father in Heaven. But, owing to the prolongation of exile and the concealment of the face, on account of our many sins, the inclination found an opening in this very thing, to cause distance between one person and his fellow in every manner that exists in reality. And one who does not labor with great exertion in this particular matter imagines that all his fellow’s toil to draw himself near to our Father in Heaven is, Heaven forbid, the opposite of this—distance from Him, blessed be He. End of quotation. And the Netziv of Volozhin, of blessed memory, wrote (the introduction to his book Haamek Davar on the Torah): The Second Temple period was a crooked and perverse generation. And we have explained that they were righteous and pious and toilers in Torah, but they were not upright in their worldly conduct. Therefore, because of baseless hatred in their hearts toward one another, they suspected anyone whom they saw conducting himself not according to their view in fear of the Lord of being a Sadducee and a heretic. And through this they came to bloodshed to an extreme degree, and to all the evils in the world, until the Temple was destroyed. And for this there was justification of the judgment: that the Holy One, blessed be He, is upright and does not tolerate tzaddikim of this sort, but only in a manner in which they walk on the upright path in worldly conduct as well, and not with crookedness, even though it is for the sake of Heaven. End of quotation.

pairs.he: ובהלכות נזקי שכנים (הלכה ה׳ אות ב׳) כתב מוהרנ״ת ז״ל: כל אחד מישראל כפי שרשו משבטו שמשם נוסח וסדר תפלתו וכפי מעשיו כן האמת שלו. ומזה נמשכים ריבוי השינויים שבין אחד לחבירו אפילו הכשרים והישרים. כי זה מתפלל בארוכה וזה במהירות זה בקול רם וזה בקול נמוך וכיוצא בזה שינויים לאין מספר אע״פ ששניהם כוונתם רצויה באמת, כי אע״פ ששניהם כוונתם באמת אעפ״כ האמת של כל אחד משונה מחבירו, ועל כן אסור לאדם להסתכל בחבירו לרעה אע״פ שנדמה לו לפי האמת שלו שחבירו אינו מתנהג באמת ואינו מתפלל באמת, כי מי יודע האמת של חבירו. כי לפי דעתו יכול לטעות שאין בחבירו אמת מחמת שאינו מתנהג כפי דעתו, אבל באמת גם חבירו כוונתו אל האמת לפי מדרגתו ושרשו. ע״כ.
pairs.en: And in Halachos of Neighbors’ Damages (Halacha 5, item 2), Moharn״Th, of blessed memory, wrote: Each person of Israel, according to his root from his tribe, from which the wording and order of his prayer come, and according to his deeds—so is his truth. And from this are drawn the many differences between one person and his fellow, even the upright and honest. For this one prays at length and this one quickly; this one aloud and this one in a low voice; and likewise differences without number, even though both their intentions are truly desired. For even though both their intentions are in truth, nevertheless the truth of each one differs from that of his fellow. And therefore a person is forbidden to look unfavorably at his fellow, even though it seems to him, according to his own truth, that his fellow does not conduct himself in truth and does not pray in truth. For who knows the truth of his fellow? For according to his own understanding he may mistakenly think that there is no truth in his fellow because he does not conduct himself according to his understanding; but in truth his fellow too directs his intention toward the truth according to his level and his root. End of quotation.

And in Halachos of Neighbors’ Damages (Halacha 5, item 2), Moharn״Th, of blessed memory, wrote: Each person of Israel, according to his root from his tribe, from which the wording and order of his prayer come, and according to his deeds—so is his truth. And from this are drawn the many differences between one person and his fellow, even the upright and honest. For this one prays at length and this one quickly; this one aloud and this one in a low voice; and likewise differences without number, even though both their intentions are truly desired. For even though both their intentions are in truth, nevertheless the truth of each one differs from that of his fellow. And therefore a person is forbidden to look unfavorably at his fellow, even though it seems to him, according to his own truth, that his fellow does not conduct himself in truth and does not pray in truth. For who knows the truth of his fellow? For according to his own understanding he may mistakenly think that there is no truth in his fellow because he does not conduct himself according to his understanding; but in truth his fellow too directs his intention toward the truth according to his level and his root. End of quotation.

pairs.en: The Ramchal wrote (Otzros HaRamchal), parsha Shemini, and these are his words: Our Sages, of blessed memory, said: Just as a bird does not fly except with its wings, so Israel cannot do anything without statutes. And the secret is this: Israel perform rectifications. But perhaps they will not rise and fly to their place, for the sitra achra would obstruct. For this the power of the statutes is needed, which actually perform the action of a bird flying with its wings; and by the power of their enactment they set up these lights to save the rectifications from the hand of the sitra achra and to raise them to their place. Thus far.

pairs.he: ועוד כתב הרמח״ל בפרשת פקודי שם: התיקונים הראשיים הם צריכים להעשות על ידי היותר חשובים שבישראל, והם מתקנים בשביל כל ישראל. ולכן בצלאל עשה המשכן שהיה משבט יהודה, החשוב שבשבטים והוא תיקן בשביל כולם. ע״כ. וכתב הרמח״ל בתיקונים חדשים (תיקון ז׳): וכל חכם לב בכם יבואו ויעשו, לאתקנא בגין כלא, ואית דאיהו לחודיה יכיל לאתקנא בגין כל ישראל, כד״א ויקם משה את המשכן, דהא כל אלין עברין אתעבידו בתיקונא דכל חד בדיליה, אבל כלא לא אשתלים ולא אתתקן אלא ע״י דמשה דאיהו שקיל ככל ישראל. מצדיקי הרבים אלין חכמי לב דאתמר דמתקני תיקוניה לכלהו ישראל, אבל המשכילים אלין משה ותרין משיחין דקיימין לאשתא על כלהו אחרנין, בגין ויביאו את המשכן אל משה, דהא איהו נטיל תדיר כל תיקונא דכלהו לאשלמא מילין כדקא יאות.
pairs.en: And the Ramchal further wrote there in the parsha Pekuday: The principal rectifications must be performed by the most distinguished among Israel, and they rectify on behalf of all Israel. And therefore Betzalel made the Tabernacle, for he was from the tribe of Yehudah, the most distinguished of the tribes, and he rectified on behalf of all of them. Thus far. And the Ramchal wrote in Tikunim Chadashim (tikun 7): “And every wise-hearted person among you shall come and make”—to rectify on behalf of all; and there is one who by himself can rectify on behalf of all Israel, as it is said, “And Moshe erected the Tabernacle.” For all these limbs were made in the rectification of each individual in his own [part], but the whole was not completed and not rectified except through Moshe, who is equal to all Israel. “Those who bring the many to righteousness”—these are the wise-hearted of whom it is said that they prepare its rectifications for all Israel; but “the enlightened”—these are Moshe and the two Messiahs who stand to oversee all the others [following the cited source; the anthology’s verb differs], because “And they brought the Tabernacle to Moshe,” for he continually takes all the rectification of them all, to complete matters as is fitting.

pairs.he: וכתב רבי אברהם אזולאי ז״ל בחסד לאברהם (מעין א׳ נהר שביעי): אפילו בדורות האחרונים כל מי שמזכך עצמו השכינה עמו, והיא נוטלת שבח כל התחתונים ושאר כשרי ישראל ותפילתם ועבודתם על ידי הכשר ההוא ראש הדגל. ע״כ. וכתב היערות דבש (חלק א׳ דרוש ט׳ לפני סופו): כמעט אבדה תקוה להעלות התפילה לשמים, אמנם בחסדו הותיר לנו שריד אשר אין דור שאין בו צדיקים מבני עליה לא יחסרו מל״ו צדיקים, א״כ כל התפלות סובבות לתפילתן של צדיקים ומתדבקות בתפילתן, והוא שאין מסך מבדיל בינו לבין השם, ע״י תפילתו גם תפילת אחרים עולה. ע״כ.
pairs.en: And Rabbi Avraham Azulai, of blessed memory, wrote in Chesed L’Avraham (spring 1, seventh stream): Even in the later generations, everyone who purifies himself has the Shechinah with him; and she takes the praise of all those below and the other upright people of Israel, and their prayer and their service, through that upright person, the head of the banner. Thus far. And Yaaros Devash wrote (Part One, discourse 9, before its conclusion): Hope of raising prayer to Heaven has nearly been lost. However, in His kindness He left us a remnant, for there is no generation in which there are not tzaddikim who are people of ascent; they will not be fewer than thirty-six tzaddikim. Therefore all the prayers revolve around the prayer of the tzaddikim and cleave to their prayer; and he is one for whom there is no screen separating him from Hashem. Through his prayer the prayer of others also rises. Thus far.

pairs.he: במגלה עמוקות כאן פרשת וישב (ויגער בו אביו) כתב: רב ברכות לראש צדיק, הן הן שלשה תפילות ביום א׳, שהוא המקבל ועושה עטרה לראש צדיק דלעילא יסוד עולם. שעל זה אמר יהודה מה בצע כי נהרוג את אחינו, ר״ל, מה נעשה מן ג׳ ברכות שבכל יום ויום שרמוזין במלת בצ״ע, ערב בוקר צהרים, ר״ל היאך יעלו ברכות שלנו בכל ג׳ תפילות שבכל יום בוקר צהרים ערבית, כשנהרוג את אחינו. כמ״ש יהודה איך אעלה אל אבי והנער איננו אתי. וכן גדול הבית צווח. הילד איננו ואני אנה אני בא, הלא דרך השער אנו נכנסים. וזה סוד כי ׳בן זקונים׳, ר״ל, מה תקנו אבות העולם שהוא התפילות, ׳הוא לו׳ הכל הולך דרך יוסף. ע״כ.
pairs.en: In Megaleh Amukos here, parsha Vayaishev (“And his father rebuked him”), he wrote: “Abundant blessings upon the head of the righteous”—these are the three prayers in one day, for he is the receiver and makes a crown for the head of the supernal tzaddik, the foundation of the world. Concerning this Yehudah said, “What profit is there if we kill our brother,” meaning: What shall we do with the three blessings that are in each and every day, which are alluded to in the word בצ״ע—“evening, morning, noon”—meaning: How will our blessings ascend in all three prayers in each day, morning, noon, evening, if we kill our brother? As Yehudah said, “How shall I go up to my father, and the youth is not with me?” And likewise the eldest of the household cries out: “The child is not here, and I, where shall I go?”—do we not enter through the gate? And this is the secret of “for [he was] a son of old age.” Meaning: What the fathers of the world instituted, namely the prayers—“he is to him”—everything goes through Yosef. Thus far.

The Ramchal wrote (Otzros HaRamchal), parsha Shemini, and these are his words: Our Sages, of blessed memory, said: Just as a bird does not fly except with its wings, so Israel cannot do anything without statutes. For this the power of the statutes is needed, which actually perform the action of a bird flying with its wings; and by the power of their enactment they set up these lights to save the rectifications from the hand of the sitra achra and to raise them to their place. Thus far.

And the Ramchal further wrote there in the parsha Pekuday: The principal rectifications must be performed by the most distinguished among Israel, and they rectify on behalf of all Israel. And therefore Betzalel made the Tabernacle, for he was from the tribe of Yehudah, the most distinguished of the tribes, and he rectified on behalf of all of them. Thus far. And the Ramchal wrote in Tikunim Chadashim (tikun 7): “And every wise-hearted person among you shall come and make”—to rectify on behalf of all; and there is one who by himself can rectify on behalf of all Israel, as it is said, “And Moshe erected the Tabernacle.” For all these limbs were made in the rectification of each individual in his own [part], but the whole was not completed and not rectified except through Moshe, who is equal to all Israel. “Those who bring the many to righteousness”—these are the wise-hearted of whom it is said that they prepare its rectifications for all Israel; but “the enlightened”—these are Moshe and the two Messiahs who stand to oversee all the others [following the cited source; the anthology’s verb differs], because “And they brought the Tabernacle to Moshe,” for he continually takes all the rectification of them all, to complete matters as is fitting.

And Rabbi Avraham Azulai, of blessed memory, wrote in Chesed L’Avraham (spring 1, seventh stream): Even in the later generations, everyone who purifies himself has the Shechinah with him; and she takes the praise of all those below and the other upright people of Israel, and their prayer and their service, through that upright person, the head of the banner. Thus far. And Yaaros Devash wrote (Part One, discourse 9, before its conclusion): Hope of raising prayer to Heaven has nearly been lost. However, in His kindness He left us a remnant, for there is no generation in which there are not tzaddikim who are people of ascent; they will not be fewer than thirty-six tzaddikim. Therefore all the prayers revolve around the prayer of the tzaddikim and cleave to their prayer; and he is one for whom there is no screen separating him from Hashem. Through his prayer the prayer of others also rises. Thus far.

In Megaleh Amukos here, parsha Vayaishev (“And his father rebuked him”), he wrote: “Abundant blessings upon the head of the righteous”—these are the three prayers in one day, for he is the receiver and makes a crown for the head of the supernal tzaddik, the foundation of the world. Concerning this Yehudah said, “What profit is there if we kill our brother,” meaning: What shall we do with the three blessings that are in each and every day, which are alluded to in the word בצ״ע—“evening, morning, noon”—meaning: How will our blessings ascend in all three prayers in each day, morning, noon, evening, if we kill our brother? As Yehudah said, “How shall I go up to my father, and the youth is not with me?” And likewise the eldest of the household cries out: “The child is not here, and I, where shall I go?”—do we not enter through the gate? And this is the secret of “for [he was] a son of old age.” Meaning: What the fathers of the world instituted, namely the prayers—“he is to him”—everything goes through Yosef. Thus far.

pairs.he: בליקוטי מוהר״ן (חלק שני סימן י׳): מה שהעולם רחוקים מהשם יתברך ואינם מתקרבים אליו יתברך, הוא רק מחמת שאין להם ישוב הדעת, ואינם מישבין עצמם. והעקר להשתדל לישב עצמו היטב. מה התכלית מכל התאוות ומכל עניני העולם הזה, הן תאוות הנכנסות לגוף, הן תאוות שחוץ לגוף, כגון כבוד, ואז בודאי ישוב אל ה׳. ע״כ.
pairs.en: In Likutay Moharan (Part Two, section 10): That people are far from Hashem, blessed be He, and do not draw near to Him, blessed be He, is only because they do not have settled understanding, and they do not settle their minds. And the essential thing is to endeavor to settle one’s mind thoroughly. What is the ultimate purpose of all the desires and of all the affairs of this world, both desires that enter the body and desires outside the body, such as honor? And then one will certainly return to Hashem. Thus far.
